problem.title: Persistent Gaps between Free $p$-Rank and Toral Rank
problem.statement: Does there exist a finite connected complex $X$ whose fundamental group is abelian and acts trivially on higher homotopy, and whose rational homotopy is finite-dimensional, such that $\operatorname{rk}_p(X)>\operatorname{rk}_T(X)$ for infinitely many primes $p$?
problem.background:
Collected from Oberwolfach Reports, which document mathematical workshops and their open-problem discussions.

**Source report:** [Cohomology of Finite Groups: Interactions and Applications (2011), Oberwolfach Reports, DOI 10.4171/owr/2010/32, pp. 1885--1952](https://doi.org/10.4171/owr/2010/32)

## Literature review (checked 2026-08-21)

**Status:** open

**Assessment.** The report explicitly labels the existence of a finite complex with free p-rank exceeding free toral rank for infinitely many primes as an open question; the cited asymptotic theorem does not settle it.

**Sources checked.**

- [Oberwolfach Report 32, Cohomology of Finite Groups](https://doi.org/10.4171/owr/2010/32)
- [Hanke, The stable free rank of symmetry of products of spheres](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00222-009-0197-3)

This is a dated literature triage derived from the supplied OWR curation; verify time-sensitive status and cited claims independently.
